dylan: Heads up — after the kernel-chooser rollout to canary pool-3 (last night) I'm seeing a 7-12% increase p50 host CPU on ingress and a noticeable smallwrite tail on gRPC. Anyone else?

emma: Yup. I replayed traffic from 02:00-03:00 and the tokenization stage moved from ~12% CPU to ~20%. Flamegraph points at token_front::split and utf8::normalize.

kai: Interesting — kernel chooser changed the microkernel path for short sequences to favor the 'fast-path' that avoids vectorized utf8 helpers. That reduces decode cost in steady state but might add extra branching/stretch for fragmented frames.

lee: I captured a quick perf sample on canary host (attached snippet):
```
# perf top -p <pid>
  token_front::split  19.5%
  grpc::write_small  11.1%
  http2::frame_unwrap 7.8%
  kv_cache::lookup    6.3%
```

dylan: benchbot replay shows KV hit-rate stable, so not a kvcache coldstart. The latency delta looks correlated with number of writes emitted per request (microframes).

benchbot: replay summary: 10k requests, baseline p50=42ms p99=240ms; post-roll p50=46ms p99=320ms. Weighted smallwrite count per request up ~18%.

emma: I also ran a quick trace with the stream-sampler. The preparse stage now does an extra memcpy for fragment stitching on ~35% of requests due to the changed kernel choosing smaller fragment windows. That explains extra smallwrite churn.

kai: Kernel chooser committed a heuristics tweak: prefer mini-batch-friendly kernel when seq_len<=24 and fragments<=3. Seems to increase framing fragmentation for HTTP/2 keepalive bursts.

lee: Two quick mitigations to try: revert the chooser change on canary, or tweak batcher hint to prefer coalesce-window=64 for that pool. Which do we want first?

dylan: Revert on canary, then run controlled replay with coalesce-window experiments. I don't want everyone chasing knobs until we confirm.

emma: Agreed. Rolling revert (canary only) now.

infra-bot: canary pool-3 rollback started by emma at 2026-03-23T12:14:02Z — status: in_progress.

kai: While that's rolling, can someone capture a pprof heap/CPU snapshot during a replay run where we toggle kernel chooser to the new policy? I want to see stack differences for tokenization vs kernel dispatch.

lee: I'll schedule a replay with tags: "kernel:new" and "kernel:old" and collect pprof at steady-state 5m windows. Also enabling stream-sampler traces at debug level for 1 minute.

dylan: Also add small instrumentation: count number of emitted writev ops per request (inet_layer.writev_count). If that goes up we can correlate to grpc smallwrite tail.

emma: Quick note — I reproduced locally by forcing chooser -> fast-path and running microbench harness. Patch shows ~9% higher host CPU vs vectorized path for our real-ish payload shapes. Repro script: 
```bash
# repro harness
./tools/replay --trace corpus/ingress/2026-03-22.json --chooser fast-path --pprof /tmp/pprof.fast
```

kai: Good repro. That suggests the branch misprediction/memcopy tradeoff is losing for our fragmentation distribution. We might need a hybrid: chooser picks fast-path only if fragment_count==1 and avg_seq_len>12.

lee: After revert completes, I'll run the replay A/B with the hybrid condition. If that fixes CPU without hurting GPU decode paths, we can ship a targeted chooser update.

infra-bot: rollback completed at 2026-03-23T12:18:34Z — canary pool-3 on kernel-chooser:v1.9.2 (previous).

dylan: Thanks. Next steps: 1) lee runs A/B with the hybrid heuristic + collects pprof and writev_count; 2) kai drafts hybrid heuristic and a unit test for fragment stats; 3) emma runs longer replay (1h) to validate p99.

emma: I'll run the 1h replay tonight and post numbers tomorrow morning. If p99 still regresses we'll open a rollback for prod.

kai: I'll open a PR with the hybrid heuristic + bench results. Title: "chooser: hybrid fast-path gating by fragment_count and seq_len".

lee: Dropping links here after runs: flamegraphs + raw perf logs (short-lived links): https://perf.redwood/dev/2812345678/flame_v_old.svg , https://perf.redwood/dev/2812345678/flame_v_new.svg

dylan: Perfect. Thanks team — nice catch before prod. :thumbsup:

lee: small follow-up: consider adding a kvcache-prefetch hint when chooser picks the fast-path so we reduce round-trips for requests that are likely to fragment. Might shave off some smallwrite ops.

kai: Nice idea. Add as follow-up once hybrid lands.

emma: Will monitor overnight and post consolidated numbers in #eng-runtime tomorrow.

lee: Closing thread for now — reopen if new signals crop up.
